title: Changeling
summary: A faerie soul that survives by living inside a mortal body, half in the everyday world and half in the Dreaming.

claims.text: The fae began to wear human bodies as armour once the weight of the mortal world grew too much for them to bear in their own forms.
Ordinary mortals see only the human; the faerie form shows only to beings of the Dreaming.
A changeling who leans too far toward mortal life withers under Banality, and one who leans too far into the Dreaming slides into Bedlam.

title: Kithain
summary: The changelings as a people, the faerie souls of the Dreaming who now live in mortal flesh, sorted into kith.

claims.text: The core book describes thirteen kith in all: boggans, clurichaun, eshu, nockers, piskies, pooka, redcaps, satyrs, selkies, two kinds of sidhe, sluagh and trolls.
Kithain society is loosely feudal, run by quarrelling noble houses and split between the Seelie and Unseelie Courts.

title: The Dreaming
summary: A world built out of human imagination and dreams, reached by changelings for adventure and for the dreamstuff of chimera.

claims.text: The book defines the Dreaming as a realm made from the dreams and imagination of humankind.
It has three broad depths: the Near Dreaming closest to the waking world, the Far Dreaming between, and the Deep Dreaming furthest away.
Book Three of the core book is given over to the Dreaming and what lives there.

title: The Near Dreaming
summary: The part of the Dreaming closest to mortal reality, where most changeling travel happens.

claims.text: The Near Dreaming is the band of the Dreaming that lies nearest the waking world.
The Far Dreaming sits between it and the Deep Dreaming.

title: The Deep Dreaming
summary: The depths of the Dreaming least tied to mortal reality, where Arcadia lies somewhere.

claims.text: The Deep Dreaming is the region of the Dreaming with the weakest bond to the waking world.
Arcadia is said to lie somewhere within it.

title: Arcadia
summary: The lost homeland of the fae, somewhere in the Deep Dreaming, where the nobles fled when the gates closed.

claims.text: Arcadia is the birthplace of the fae and lies somewhere in the Deep Dreaming.
During the Shattering most ruling fae escaped there through the last open gate and left the commoners behind.
Sidhe came back out of Arcadia at the Resurgence, when the gates opened again in 1969.

title: The Autumn World
summary: The changelings' name for the mundane mortal world, grown cold with Banality.

claims.text: The book calls the mortal world the Autumn world throughout its history of the fae.
Invoking the Autumn is a rule for calling on Banality's power on purpose.

title: Glamour
summary: The stuff of dreams and wonder that feeds the fae and fuels their magic; one of a changeling's Tempers.

claims.text: Mortals are named as the main source of Glamour in the world, even as they are also the source of Banality.
Glamour is spent on cantrips and other faerie effects, and its uses and how it is regained are set out with the other traits.
Changelings take in Glamour through five kinds of Epiphany.

title: Banality
summary: The cold, deadening force of disbelief that opposes Glamour and slowly erodes a changeling's faerie self.

claims.text: Banality works against Glamour; a little keeps a changeling grounded, but a high rating is a danger.
The core book gives rules for its effects, for gaining it and for shedding it.
Too much Banality can make a changeling forget their faerie nature and live as an ordinary mortal.

title: Bedlam
summary: The madness that takes a changeling who touches the Dreaming too deeply, losing hold of both worlds.

claims.text: Bedlam is defined as a madness that cuts a changeling off from mundane reality after too strong a contact with the Dreaming.
Its rules, and the road toward the endless dream, come at the close of the systems chapter.

title: The Chrysalis
summary: The moment a sleeping faerie soul wakes and a mortal becomes a changeling.

claims.text: The Chrysalis is the awakening of the fae soul inside a mortal.
Children who carry a fae soul often seem odd long before it, drawn to monsters, far lands and wonder tales.
A changeling fresh from the Chrysalis is called a fledge.

title: The Changeling Way
summary: The ritual that bound faerie souls to mortal bodies so they could survive the Banality of the mortal world.

claims.text: Fae who could not reach Arcadia at the Shattering took the Changeling Way and joined their souls to mortal ones.
After that first generation died, their souls were reborn into mortal children, which is how changelings come to be born today.
Some Arcadian sidhe take mortal form by other means.

title: Chimera
summary: Dreamstuff: creatures, objects and places made of dreams, real to the fae and unseen by mortals.

claims.text: Chimera make up the fabric of the Dreaming itself, whether as beasts, objects or parts of the landscape.
The chimerical quality of the world is explained early in Chapter One.

title: The Mists
summary: The forgetfulness that hides chimerical events from mortals and from changelings caught by Banality.

claims.text: The Mists are introduced as part of the nature of the fae and treated in more depth with the Banality rules.

title: Fae Mien and Mortal Seeming
summary: A changeling's true faerie look, seen by other fae, and the human face the mortal world sees.

claims.text: The fae mien is the changeling's true appearance; ordinary mortals cannot usually see it.
Mortal seeming and fae mien are covered together in Chapter One.
A changeling has both at once rather than switching between them.

title: Seeming
summary: The three stages of a changeling's faerie life: childling, wilder and grump.

claims.text: Childlings are marked by curiosity and a wish for adventure; wilders by a drive to explore and test limits.
The three seemings, childling, wilder and grump, each get their own write-up in Chapter Two.
How changelings age is set out in Chapter One.

title: Fosterage
summary: The time after the Chrysalis when an older changeling teaches a new one how to live as fae.

claims.text: Fosterage follows the Chrysalis in the book's account of the nature of the fae.

title: The Courts
summary: Kithain politics turns on two rival Courts, Seelie and Unseelie, with a hidden Shadow Court beside them.

claims.text: The Seelie and Unseelie Courts are named as the two largest governing bodies of the Kithain.
Chapter One follows the Courts through the ages, then covers attitudes, membership and each Court in turn.

title: The Seelie Court
summary: The Court of tradition, honour and chivalry, which led Concordia through most of modern history.

claims.text: The Seelie Court and its Code are described in Chapter One.
House Gwydion sees itself as the head of the Seelie, as House Ailil does of the Unseelie.

title: The Unseelie Court
summary: The Court of change, passion and freedom, which keeps its own Code against the Seelie one.

claims.text: The Unseelie Court and its Code are described in Chapter One.
House Ailil claims to lead the Unseelie and justifies its schemes as restoring the balance of the Courts.

title: The Shadow Court
summary: A secret, darker body behind the Unseelie Court, linked in rumour to House Ailil.

claims.text: The Shadow Court has its own section after the two open Courts.
Many fae believe every Ailil has a hand in it, though the book says the belief goes too far.

title: The Escheat
summary: The highest law of the Kithain, sworn between the Seelie and Unseelie Courts.

claims.text: The Escheat is the oldest law shared by both Courts.

title: Noble Houses
summary: The great sidhe houses that rule Kithain society, each with its own court, gift and flaw.

claims.text: Chapter Two gives fourteen houses: Aesin, Ailil, Balor, Beaumayn, Danaan, Daireann, Dougal, Eiluned, Fiona, Gwydion, Leanhaun, Liam, Scathach and Varich.
Each house entry gives a boon and a flaw for its members.

title: House Aesin
summary: A house bound to nature and beasts, who see themselves as guardians of the Dreaming.

claims.text: Members can speak with animals, and many feel a bond to one animal in particular.
Outsiders often take them for savages, but they think of themselves as the last true keepers of fae society.

title: House Ailil
summary: The Dragons: masters of politics and manipulation who claim the leadership of the Unseelie Court.

claims.text: Ailil are known as leaders, planners and manipulators, and other houses fear crossing them.
The house sees itself as head of the Unseelie Court.

title: House Balor
summary: An Unseelie house whose members carry visible deformities from their Fomorian heritage.

claims.text: Balor deformities give no rules benefit on their own and show up in the mortal seeming as something odd but natural.
Witnesses find a Balor hard to forget, which makes them easier to trace.

title: House Beaumayn
summary: A house of seers and occult seekers, many of whom dream true even before their Chrysalis.

claims.text: Beaumayn are often drawn early to the occult and to the hidden history of where they live.
Unseelie members of the house are uncommon.

title: House Danaan
summary: The Pathfinders: a small house scattered across worlds, open to commoners in its ranks.

claims.text: Danaan is the only noble house led by a High Lord who is not sidhe.
The house dislikes the mortal world and admits commoner kith such as eshu, satyrs, piskies and nockers.

title: House Daireann
summary: A house known for its custom of hospitality and its sworn societies of herbalists and fighters.

claims.text: Its societies include poison makers, an oathbound order of fighters and the keepers of the cauldronhouses, wayhouses open to all.

title: House Dougal
summary: The Smiths: makers whose bodies slowly take on the craft, piece by piece.

claims.text: Each level of Title brings a working artificial part to a Dougal's body, such as a clockwork eye or a brass hand.

title: House Eiluned
summary: The House of Secrets: a house of magic and prophecy founded by Ailil's sister.

claims.text: The founder Eiluned was the sister of Ailil and warned the sidhe of a coming darkness; the warning went unheeded and split the two.
The house readied strongholds before the Sundering.
Gwydion's truth-sensing gift does not work on Eiluned.

title: House Fiona
summary: The Lions: a Seelie house of fierce love, loyalty and reckless daring.

claims.text: Fiona belong to the Seelie Court and value true love above all.
They court danger for its own sake.
Fiona demanded a hearing and punishment after the Beltaine Massacre, and no one listened.

title: House Gwydion
summary: A proud Seelie house of rulers and warriors that clings hardest to the old order.

claims.text: A Gwydion can sense lies with a Perception and Kenning roll.
Its flaw is an honour that cannot let an insult pass unavenged.
The High King Dafyll who led the war against the commoners was of this house.

title: House Leanhaun
summary: The Muses: an Unseelie house that shapes culture and feeds on the inspiration of mortals.

claims.text: Leanhaun seek jobs that bring them many potential Dreamers, such as agents, scouts and art teachers.
They play a long game of shaping culture through books, songs and films.

title: House Liam
summary: An exiled house that stood between mortals and the fae and stayed behind at the Shattering.

claims.text: Its founder King Liam believed the new Christian faith held the same creative spark as art and song.
Liam and Scathach nobles took the Changeling Way and remained in the mortal world when the other nobles fled.

title: House Scathach
summary: The Gray Walkers: a house of warriors and agents with a bad name among nobles, who stayed behind at the Shattering.

claims.text: Scathach suffer a +2 difficulty on Social rolls with most nobles and royalist commoners; Liam and Danaan nobles are exempt.
Gray Walkers who are Autumn sidhe or other kith are barred from using Sovereign by an old pact.
Scathach nobles were among those who stayed in the mortal world through the Interregnum.

title: House Varich
summary: The Puppetmasters: a house that reads patterns and predicts what others will do.

claims.text: Given time to study, a Varich can foresee outcomes such as markets, card hands or duels.

title: Households and Motleys
summary: The small groups changelings live in: households under one roof, and motleys bound by shared purpose.

claims.text: Changeling society is described through households, motleys, and the bond of liege and vassal.

title: Liege and Vassal
summary: The feudal oaths that tie commoners and nobles together in Kithain society.

claims.text: Liege and vassal ties are set out as part of changeling society.
The book's sample oaths include oaths of fealty.

title: Freeholds
summary: Places soaked in Glamour where changelings meet and live, with a balefire at their heart.

claims.text: A freehold is a place full of Glamour used as a home and meeting place.
The balefire is the part of a freehold where its Glamour gathers and is kept.

title: Glades
summary: Wild places rich in Glamour, out in nature rather than tied to a court.

claims.text: Glades are listed first among the places of Glamour.

title: Trods
summary: Faerie roads that link freeholds and places of Glamour.

claims.text: Trods are described with glades and freeholds among the places of Glamour.

title: Kingdom of Concordia
summary: The great changeling realm of North America, ruled by a High King from Tara-Nar.

claims.text: Concordia is split into kingdoms such as Apples, Willows, Grass, the Burning Sun and Pacifica, each given a short write-up.
Commoners left in Concordia at the Shattering built their own rule before the sidhe came back.

title: Tara-Nar
summary: The capital of Concordia, the High King's seat.

claims.text: Tara-Nar is named the capital of the western world.

title: Changeling Realms Abroad
summary: The changeling kingdoms of Europe and the wider world, from Albion and Hibernia to the Empire of the Firebird.

claims.text: Chapter One sketches realms across the world, among them Albion, Hibernia, Caledonia, Cymru, Neustria, Iberia, the Hellenic Empire and the Empire of the Firebird.

title: The Mythic Age
summary: The ancient time when fae and mortals shared the world freely and Glamour was everywhere.

claims.text: Kithain history opens with the Mythic Age.

title: The Sundering
summary: The first great break between the fae and the mortal world, as Banality grew.

claims.text: The Sundering follows the Mythic Age in the book's history.
House Eiluned saw it coming and fortified its freeholds in advance.

title: The Shattering
summary: The closing of the gates to Arcadia, when the nobles fled and the commoners were left behind.

claims.text: From the 14th century the gates broke one after another as faith and reason drove out old beliefs.
Fae chose between sealing themselves into their realms, fleeing to Arcadia, or taking the Changeling Way.
Those who sealed themselves away went mad on their own Glamour and became Lost Ones.

title: The Interregnum
summary: The long centuries when the commoners ran fae society alone, without the Arcadian nobles.

claims.text: The Interregnum runs from the Shattering until the sidhe returned, through world wars and the Depression.
Changelings who fought in the world wars often came home Undone.

title: The Resurgence
summary: The return of the Arcadian sidhe in 1969, when human hope reopened the way.

claims.text: After the Second World War, new dreams of space and the future sent Glamour back into the Dreaming.
The gates to Arcadia opened again on July 20, 1969.
Returning nobles found commoners who had done well without them.

title: The Night of Iron Knives
summary: The Beltaine Massacre, when sidhe murdered commoner leaders at a peace feast and set off the Accordance War.

claims.text: Arcadian sidhe invited commoner leaders to a Beltaine masquerade to talk peace, and masked killers with cold iron knives slew them.
House Fiona's calls for an inquiry went unheard and war followed.

title: The Accordance War
summary: The war between returning nobles and commoners that ended with David crowned High King.

claims.text: Ten days after the massacre the nobles marched under High King Dafyll of House Gwydion and took San Francisco in the Battle of the Bay.
The war ran alongside the mortal Vietnam war.
Queen Mab acknowledged David as High King after a sign from the Dreaming confirmed a prophecy.

title: The Evanescence
summary: The surge of nightmare Glamour around September 11, 2001 that let many Thallain into the Autumn world.

claims.text: The Evanescence is dated to around September 11, 2001.
It brought nightmarish Glamour into the mortal world and opened the way for Thallain.

title: Concordia in the Present Day
summary: A troubled realm with a returned but broken High King and rival claims to power.

claims.text: David returned from the Dreaming and spoke to the Parliament of Dreams, then withdrew, troubled by chaotic dreams.
In the High King's absence conservative Arcadian sidhe gained influence through bribes and threats.

title: High King David
summary: The young sidhe crowned High King of Concordia, who vanished and later came back changed.

claims.text: David bore Caliburn and was recognised by Queen Mab after a griffon shielded the boy at the court.
David tried to make peace with the commoners after the Accordance War.
David went missing for years, then returned older and troubled.

title: High King Dafyll
summary: The House Gwydion war leader who led the nobles at the start of the Accordance War.

claims.text: Dafyll, the war leader of House Gwydion, carried Caliburn and took San Francisco within a week.

title: Queen Mab
summary: A great noble of Concordia whose blessing made David's rule secure.

claims.text: Mab first refused to accept David, then proclaimed the young noble High King after the prophecy came true.
During David's absence Mab backed Princess Lenore and accused Faerilyth of a part in the disappearance.

title: Faerilyth
summary: David's queen, whose claim to rule was denied while David was missing.

claims.text: Faerilyth set up court in the Kingdom of Willows during David's absence, and Mab and Morwen both refused to call Faerilyth High Queen.
Faerilyth embraced David on the High King's return to the Parliament of Dreams.

title: Thallain
summary: Fae born of nightmare and darkness, enemies of the Kithain.

claims.text: The Evanescence let many Thallain into the Autumn world.
Thallain are named across the book among the darker beings of the Dreaming.

title: Dauntain
summary: Changelings with broken faerie souls who hunt Glamour and other fae.

claims.text: Dauntain carry old Brands that twist them, and they corrupt, torment and destroy Glamour and the Dreaming.

title: The Enchanted and Kinain
summary: Mortals given Glamour so they can see the Dreaming, and mortals with faerie blood.

claims.text: The Enchanted are mortals filled with Glamour, chiefly so they can perceive the Dreaming.
Kinain, kin of the fae, appear throughout the book as mortals tied to changeling families.

title: Gallain
summary: Creatures of the Dreaming that are not Kithain, such as the Nunnehi, the Inanimae and the Adhene.

claims.text: Gallain means any being of the Dreaming outside the Kithain.
The Nunnehi of the Americas and the Inanimae, fae of objects and places, are among them.

title: Lost Ones
summary: Fae who sealed themselves into their realms at the Shattering and went mad from their own Glamour.

claims.text: Fae who locked themselves inside unchanging realms during the Shattering became Lost Ones.

title: Boggans
summary: Hard-working, hospitable kith who love simple comforts and always know the court gossip.

claims.text: Boggans prize work and hospitality and are famed for honesty.
Boggans know the latest court rumours better than anyone.

title: Clurichaun
summary: Music-loving kith from Ireland, the truth behind the leprechaun tale.

claims.text: Mortal stories of leprechauns come from garbled tales of clurichaun.
Most live in Ireland, and some came to American cities with Irish migrants.

title: Eshu
summary: Wanderers and storytellers who cannot resist the open road.

claims.text: Eshu take their name from a Yoruba trickster and messenger spirit.
They first arose from the dreams of the nomads of Chaldea.
An eshu remembers every story heard.

title: Nockers
summary: Bitter, sarcastic master crafters who want everything perfect.

claims.text: Nockers are known as much for cynicism as for skill at making things.
They prefer mechanical wonders to people.

title: Piskies
summary: Quick, friendly couriers of the Dreaming who keep what they pocket.

claims.text: Piskies carry messages, parcels and secrets between courts and commoners.
Piskies tend to be solitary wanderers.

title: Pooka
summary: Pranksters and jesters, each bonded to one kind of animal.

claims.text: Pooka love pranks and hate meanness and hard work.
Every pooka shares a close bond with a particular animal.

title: Redcaps
summary: Kith born of nightmare, the terror of fae children and rebels against any ruler.

claims.text: Redcaps are named for caps dipped in enemies' blood in older days.
Redcaps delight in disgusting or frightening others and oppose whoever rules.

title: Satyrs
summary: Passionate kith devoted to pleasure, revel and appetite.

claims.text: Satyrs pursue their desires without restraint and have the stamina for days of revel.

title: Selkies
summary: Seal-folk of the sea, loving and distant, bound to their seal coats.

claims.text: Selkies are both seal and human, and guarding the seal coat shapes their wariness.

title: Arcadian Sidhe
summary: The noble sidhe who fled to Arcadia and returned at the Resurgence.

claims.text: The returning sidhe found commoners who had thrived without them.
They are more fragile against Banality than commoners and lean on old customs.

title: Autumn Sidhe
summary: Sidhe of Houses Liam and Scathach who stayed in the mortal world through the Interregnum.

claims.text: Liam and Scathach nobles took the Changeling Way rather than flee, and greeted the returning sidhe in 1969.

title: Sluagh
summary: Secretive collectors of secrets and lost lore who live in old, dark places.

claims.text: Sluagh are called the underfolk; a few live in tunnels and sewers, most in old mansions or stone buildings.
Sluagh gather secrets and forgotten lore.

title: Trolls
summary: Honourable guardians whose strength fails them if they break their word.

claims.text: Trolls come from dreams of warriors and guardians and serve as protectors of the courts.
A troll who breaks an oath sickens until the dishonour is redeemed.

title: Kith Creation
summary: Rules for building a new kith: concept, role in the Dreaming, birthrights, frailty and affinity.

claims.text: New kith are built in six steps, from concept and role through birthrights, frailty and affinity to adjustment.
A worked example builds a kith from the domovoi.

title: Arts
summary: The schools of faerie magic, from Chicanery and Primal to Sovereign and Wayfare.

claims.text: Chapter Four lists eighteen Arts: Autumn, Chicanery, Chronos, Contract, Dragon's Ire, Legerdemain, Metamorphosis, Naming, Oneiromancy, Primal, Pyretics, Skycraft, Soothsay, Sovereign, Spring, Summer, Wayfare and Winter.
Scathach who are not Arcadian sidhe may not use Sovereign under an old pact.

title: Realms
summary: The second half of a cantrip: what it can affect, from people to places and time.

claims.text: There are six Realms: Actor, Fae, Nature, Prop, Scene and Time.
A cantrip joins an Art with a Realm.

title: Cantrips
summary: Faerie spells: an Art and a Realm joined by Glamour.

claims.text: A cantrip is a spell made with Glamour from an Art and a Realm.
Cantrip casting is explained at the start of Chapter Four.

title: Bunks
summary: Actions a changeling performs to trigger or ease a cantrip.

claims.text: A bunk is an action done to activate a cantrip or make it easier.

title: Unleashing
summary: Letting raw Glamour loose without a cantrip's shape, with unpredictable results.

claims.text: Unleashing is treated after cantrips and bunks in Chapter Four.

title: Tempers
summary: A changeling's three pools: Glamour, Willpower and Banality.

claims.text: Tempers, converting points between them, Willpower and Glamour each get a section in Chapter Six.
Tempers are set during character creation, step four.

title: Invoking the Wyrd
summary: Making chimerical effects real in the mortal world, at a cost.

claims.text: Invoking the Wyrd is covered in the Tempers section.

title: Epiphany
summary: The five ways a changeling gains Glamour: Rapture, Ravaging, Rhapsody, Revelry and Reverie.

claims.text: Epiphany takes five forms: Rapture, Ravaging, Rhapsody, Revelry and Reverie.
Ravaging is the cruel way, taking Glamour by force from mortals.

title: Dreamers
summary: Mortals whose creativity feeds changelings with Glamour, and a Background that stands for them.

claims.text: Dreamers is one of the changeling Backgrounds.
Leanhaun look for jobs that bring many Dreamers within reach.

title: Oaths
summary: Binding promises sworn under the Dreaming, with penalties for breaking them.

claims.text: Chapter Six covers swearing an oath, restoration and atonement, and gives sample oaths.
Trolls suffer especially when they break an oath.

title: Cold Iron
summary: The bane of the fae: wounds from cold iron are especially dangerous to changelings.

claims.text: Cold iron has its own rules in the Health section.
The Beltaine Massacre was done with cold iron knives.

title: Nightmare
summary: A measure of how far a changeling's Glamour has turned dark.

claims.text: Nightmare has its own section in Chapter Six, before combat.

title: Kenning and Gremayre
summary: The two changeling Abilities: a Talent for sensing Glamour and a Knowledge of faerie lore.

claims.text: Kenning is a changeling Talent and Gremayre a changeling Knowledge.
House Gwydion uses Perception and Kenning to tell truth from lies.

title: Changeling Backgrounds
summary: Traits such as Chimera, Dreamers, Holdings, Remembrance, Retinue, Title and Treasures.

claims.text: The Backgrounds are Chimera, Contacts, Dreamers, Holdings, Mentor, Remembrance, Resources, Retinue, Title and Treasures, and they can be pooled.

title: Legacies
summary: Paired Seelie and Unseelie personality archetypes that every changeling carries.

claims.text: Legacies come in Seelie and Unseelie sets, each with its own quest and ban.
Seelie examples include Courtier, Paladin and Troubadour; Unseelie include Fool, Rogue and Riddler.

title: Threshold and Antithesis
summary: A creation step that names what draws a changeling's Glamour and what threatens it.

claims.text: Threshold and Antithesis are step eight of character creation.
